subject: DONE s337 (1b0a7e4): read-only arrays — SvREADONLY is a macro, the flag IS the storage (simple vector)
description:
SHIPPED s337, commit 1b0a7e4.  Option (b) as ruled: `Internals::SvREADONLY(@a,1)` swaps the variable's storage for a SIMPLE vector (no fill pointer, not adjustable) over the same element boxes = perl's fixed-size AV whose ELEMENTS stay writable.  Size changes fail by construction; guards only supply perl's "Modification of a read-only value attempted".

HOW THE CELL WAS REACHED (caveat (i) of the ruling): `Internals::pl-SvREADONLY` is now a MACRO in the Internals package — the codegen already emits the array VARIABLE, so the call site holds the storage cell.  Zero Pl/ change.  Anything not a `@`-symbol routes to %p-svreadonly-other, which announces + no-ops.

Caveat (ii), the adjustability audit: done.  Guards added at p-push-impl (via %p-push-cold), p-unshift, p-pop, p-shift, p-splice-impl, p-array-fill, p-array-deref-=, p-undef, p-array-set / p-aref / p-aref-box / the two autoviv-aref extend branches, p-delete-array + both delete-slices, p-set-array-length (grow).  Everything else that touches fill-pointer operates on freshly-made local vectors.

Perl asymmetries implemented: `push @ro, ()` allowed (nothing stored) while `unshift @ro, ()` dies; a no-op splice dies; out-of-bounds element write dies, in-bounds does not.

FIXED ON THE WAY: %p-defelem-box's setter gated its in-bounds branch on `fill-pointer` where it meant `length`, so the hole-vivify write was dropped for any vector without one.

DIVERGENCES (announced once per kind, never silent — rule-12 effect-only boundary), all written up in not-supported.md §Internals::*: shrinking `$#ro=N` (perl truncates; a simple vector cannot be truncated in place and the cell is not reachable there), a ref taken BEFORE the swap (keeps the old adjustable vector — CL cannot un-adjust an array), `SvREADONLY(@$ref,1)`, and the still-unimplemented read-only SCALAR / restricted HASH forms.

TESTS: push.t 32/0, unshift.t 19/0, splice.t 34/0 fully passing; sort.t's in-place-sort row passes (its one fail, t177 AUTOLOAD, is the blessed baseline row).  BOTH skip-registry entries deleted (comments left in place saying not to re-register).  The hand-edited `ok(1,"SKIP")` stubs in perl-tests/splice.t AND perl-tests/sort.t restored from the t/op originals — the sort.t one was not in this task, found by grepping for the feature.

Guard: Pl/t/readonly-array-01.t, 18 rows, every expectation taken from perl 5.40 running the same program (incl. inverse guard that a plain array still push/pop/splice/extends).

Gate 131/4594 PASS.  Sweep 18477 passing / 679 fails, GATE clean, 0 new / 2 fixed.  Emission byte-identical — no gen bump, no artifact regeneration.
